metadata.document: Feedback on the Draft Auckland Unitary Plan

cleaned_body_text: Feedback on the Draft Auckland Unitary Plan. TO: Auckland Unitary Plan Feedback Team, Auckland Council, Freepost 237170, Private Bag 92300, Auckland 1142. FROM: Environmental Defence Society Inc, PO Box 91736, Victoria St West, Auckland 1142. 1. INTRODUCTION. 1.1 The Environmental Defence Society (“EDS”) welcomes the opportunity to comment on the Draft Auckland Unitary Plan (“the Draft Plan”). 1.2 EDS is a not-for-profit national environmental advocacy group established in 1971 to advocate for better environmental outcomes in resource management matters. 2. LEGAL FRAMEWORK. 2.1 The key environmental provisions with which the Unitary Plan must comply are set out below. Part 2 of the RMA: The purpose of the RMA is the sustainable management of natural and physical resources (section 5). The Draft Plan must achieve this purpose, as well as recognise and provide for matters of national importance (sections 6 and 7). EDS draws attention to section 7(f): the requirement to have particular regard to the maintenance and enhancement of the quality of the environment. 3. GENERAL COMMENTS. Format: We are impressed by the electronic format developed for the plan and find it to be a useful and user-friendly means of navigating an extremely complex document. Intent: EDS supports the intention of the Draft Plan to deliver the vision for Auckland set out in the Auckland Plan. Overall, EDS considers that the Draft Plan proposes an appropriate balance between providing for Auckland’s growing population and protecting natural values. Loss of local planning detail: EDS has deep concerns about the loss of local-scale planning provisions in some areas, including the West Coast Rural Policy Area, Swanson Structure Plan, and Long Bay structure plan. Drafting: We are concerned that condensing provisions has resulted in the loss of key principles and that frequent use of vague wording does not create a clear imperative for action. 4. CONTENT. Urban form: EDS supports the proposal to provide for 60-70 per cent of total new dwellings up to 2040 within the existing metropolitan area. Freshwater: EDS’s key concern in relation to freshwater is ensuring the Draft Plan gives effect to the NPSFM and the Council’s functions. Biodiversity: A whole-of-region approach and a no-net loss approach should be applied to maintain indigenous biodiversity. Rural development: EDS largely supports the provisions in the plan related to rural development. Landscape and natural character: We are concerned to note that there are no objectives and policies included in section 3 of the Draft Plan in relation to ONLs, ONCs and HNCs. Coastal: EDS supports the intention of the plan to avoid coastal subdivision and development outside of established settlements. Marine: EDS supports provisions related to the protection of the Hauraki Gulf Marine Park but emphasizes that the west coast must also be protected.
